title: THE LORD, THE GOD OF ISRAEL

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: This is the inheritance Moses had given when he was in the plains of Moab across the Jordan east of Jericho. But to the tribe of Levi, Moses had given no inheritance; the Lord, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he promised them - Josh 13:32-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes exactly where its heart has been all along. After all the boundaries and towns and tribal portions, the final word returns to Levi — the tribe with no land — and states it once more: "the Lord, the God of Israel, is their inheritance." Scripture repeats it so we will not miss it. The greatest possession is God Himself.

The other tribes could point to their fields and say, "This is mine." But when disaster came, when enemies invaded, when crops failed, land could be lost. The Levites' inheritance could never be taken away, because their inheritance was the living God. What a secure portion that was — richer and safer than any acreage in Canaan.

This is where the whole chapter has been leading us. Land matters, provision matters, and God gives these things generously. But every earthly portion is temporary. The one inheritance that cannot fade, spoil, or be stolen is God Himself, kept for us in Christ (1 Pet 1:4). In Jesus, the privilege once reserved for Levi becomes ours: we are brought near, made God's own, given the Lord Himself as our eternal portion. Whatever else you may or may not have in this life, if you have Christ, you have the inheritance that outlasts everything.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- If you lost every earthly possession, would you still count yourself rich in God?
- How does an inheritance that cannot be taken away change your sense of security?
- What would it mean to truly treasure the Lord as your portion this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are my inheritance, and You can never be taken from me. When earthly things prove temporary, help me to rest in the eternal portion I have in You through Christ. Amen.
